Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital identity systems and credentials. 30 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether the system enables individuals to authenticate themselves or their documents digitally through electronic verification
Comments: Yes. The CEDEAO biometric ID card contains an NFC chip enabling digital authentication. Multiple commercial KYC providers (Uqudo, Smile ID, VOVE ID) confirm NFC chip reading and digital verification against the card. The 2022 INN project explicitly aims to 'facilitate authentication of citizens' digitally. The Senegal Services portal and e-tax platform require digital identity for access. The INN feasibility study describes an authentication module as a core component of the planned digital ID architecture.

Definition: Whether individuals can view their data held in the ID database and see how it has been accessed
Comments: Yes. Law 2008-12 grants individuals the right to access and obtain a copy of their personal data from data controllers, including the right to know what data is processed and why, and the right to request correction or deletion. The CDP enforces these rights. Citizens can lodge complaints with the CDP if their data access rights are not respected. The Access to Information Law (2025-15) further reinforces citizens' rights to access information held by public institutions.

Definition: Whether the system enables Know Your Customer (KYC) packet collection for service provision, particularly financial services
Comments: Yes. The national ID card (CNI/CEDEAO card) is the primary KYC document in Senegal per Smile ID and VOVE ID. AML/KYC regulations enforced by CENTIF and BCEAO require financial institutions to verify customer identity using the CNI or other approved documents. Law No. 2018-03 and Law No. 02/2024 mandate risk-based Customer Due Diligence. The biometric NFC chip enables digital KYC verification. Senegal was removed from the FATF grey list in October 2024 following strengthening of its KYC/AML regime.

Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Value Name: Yes, but not specific to ID
Comments: Yes, but not ID-specific. Senegal's general judicial system provides oversight of data protection through the courts and criminal law. The CDP (Data Protection Commission) can refer breaches to the public prosecutor. The criminal code (amended 2016, 2021) provides penalties for unauthorised data processing. The Cybercrime Law (2008-10) criminalises unauthorised access to computer systems. However, there are no ID-specific judicial oversight mechanisms; oversight operates through the general legal framework and the CDP's administrative powers.

Definition: Whether the civil registration and digital ID systems are integrated
Comments: Partial integration. Senegal launched the 'Nekkal' programme (2021, EU-funded 27.4M EUR) to digitise 19M+ civil status records and interconnect civil status centres. By June 2024 the Minister announced 19M records digitised. Senegal is 'embedding CRVS within national digital identity frameworks' per the WHO/OIF 2025 roundtable. However, as of January 2026, the National Civil Status Agency (ANEC) announced deployment of birth/death pre-declaration software in health facilities is still upcoming, indicating full integration is not yet achieved. Civil registration and the biometric ID database are partially but not fully interlinked.

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: Partially available. Law 2008-12 sets rules on data sharing and trans-border transfers (CDP prior notification required). The CDP maintains a public directory of data processing operations. Senegal adopted an Access to Information Law (loi n°2025-15) in August 2025, but civil society noted it may not fully meet international standards. Data sharing rules exist for inter-ministerial and e-government use (interconnection of databases permitted for public services). However, no fully open data-sharing framework for government ID data exists, and specific rules for the biometric register sharing are not publicly detailed.

Definition: Whether specific regulation or policy addresses digital ID beyond general identification legislation
Comments: No dedicated digital ID-specific regulation as of the research period. The INN feasibility study (2022) explicitly noted the 'absence of texts defining digital identity (sectorially or nationally)' and recommended choosing between legislating specifically on the INN or complementing the existing legal framework. The general data protection law (2008-12), electronic transactions law (2008-08), and identity card regulations apply, but there is no standalone digital ID law. The New Deal Technologique (2025) calls for updating the legal/regulatory framework, suggesting it remains pending.

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: Yes. Act No. 2008-12 of 25 January 2008 on the Protection of Personal Data is in force. Implementing Decree No. 2008-721 of 30 June 2008 was issued. The Cybercrime Law (2008-10) provides additional protections. These laws entered into force in 2014 when the CDP became operational. The law covers collection, processing, transmission, storage and use of personal data including biometric data and national ID numbers, which require prior CDP authorisation.

Definition: Whether a Data Protection Authority or similar body regulates ID data collection and sharing by the ID system
Comments: Yes. The Commission de Données Personnelles (CDP) is an independent administrative authority established by Law 2008-12, composed of 11 members. It became operational in 2014. The CDP receives declarations and authorisations for personal data processing (including biometric data and national ID numbers), conducts on-site inspections, issues administrative fines (1M–100M CFA), and can suspend or withdraw processing authorisations. The RNU social registry explicitly involves CDP oversight.

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: Yes. The Senegalese national ID card (Carte Nationale d'Identité CEDEAO) is accepted as legal proof of identity. The IRB Canada (2018) document confirms the card 'is proof of identity' and 'is often required for administrative procedures or commercial transactions' and must be presented during security checks. Citizens need it for banking KYC, SIM registration, social services, and it is the sole required document for voter registration since 2021.

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: Yes. Senegal has a legal framework governing identity. The ECOWAS biometric card was introduced in law in 2016. The national ID card system is governed under the Ministry of Interior. Law No. 2008-12 on Personal Data Protection provides the overarching legal basis for data collection and processing in identity systems. The penal code (amended 2016, 2021) includes provisions on identity data. The INN feasibility study (2022) noted 'existence of a legal framework on fundamental identity.' The Senegal Digital Strategy 2025 and New Deal Technologique provide further policy frameworks.

Definition: Whether the system and the production of credentials can be managed, maintained and developed by in-country technical staff (as opposed to foreign vendors)
Comments: Partial in-country maintenance. The DAF (government) manages day-to-day operations. However, the card production and key technical infrastructure has been contracted to Iris Corporation Berhad (Malaysia) since 2016 (original $90M contract), with renewal in 2021 ($19.5M). The Feb 2026 breach showed IRIS Corporation responding first to the technical incident. Senegal Numérique SA handles some digital infrastructure. The New Deal Technologique (2025) explicitly aims to reduce reliance on foreign tech expertise, indicating current partial dependence on foreign vendors.

Definition: Whether the Ministry of Finance has oversight of the financing and development of the digital ID system
Comments: Partial oversight. The 2026 Digital Ministry budget (CFA 81.06 billion) was reviewed and adopted by the National Assembly and includes digital identity as a priority. The New Deal Technologique budget (CFA 1,105 billion) involves the Ministry of Finance. The Banking Law 2025 requires Ministry of Finance authorisation for banking activities (relevant to KYC/ID use). However, the national ID card system sits under the Ministry of Interior, not Finance. Finance oversight is partial and indirect rather than full oversight of the ID system.

Definition: Whether the ongoing management, maintenance and development of the ID system can be funded by sustainable domestic resources
Comments: Mixed financing. The Iris Corporation contract (since 2016, renewed 2021 at $19.5M) is domestically funded. The INN project (2022) had a budget of 3.2B CFA (~$5.1M) and was UNDP-supported. The New Deal Technologique ($1.7B total, 2025) has identified domestic and external sources, with Gates Foundation contributing $10M. The Nekkal civil registration digitisation was EU-funded (27.4M EUR). World Bank PAEN (2023, $150M) also supports digital infrastructure. The ID system thus relies on a mix of domestic budget and significant external donor/development bank funding.

Definition: Whether the system collects biometric data and which modalities are collected (fingerprints, facial image, iris scans)
Comments: Senegal collects fingerprints, facial images, and iris scans. The ECOWAS biometric card collects fingerprints and a facial photo. The Al Jazeera (Feb 2026) report on Senegal's biometric health card explicitly states it 'uses fingerprints, facial images and iris scans to unlock access to treatment.' The DAF biometric population register stores multi-modal biometrics.

Definition: Whether identity records are stored in electronic/digital format versus paper-based records
Comments: Senegal operates a fully digital biometric population register managed by the DAF (Directorate of File Automation). The DAF database stores biometric and biographical data electronically. The Feb 2026 cyberattack targeted this digital infrastructure, confirming it is a centralised electronic database. Additionally, over 19 million civil status records have been digitised under the 'Nekkal' programme (funded by EU, 27.4M EUR). The INN project (2022–2024) further builds the digital identity database.

Definition: Whether the digital ID system is designed to be interoperable across government agencies and with other systems through APIs or data exchange protocols
Comments: Yes — partial/growing interoperability. Senegal Numérique SA partnered with the African Digital Development Agency (ADD) specifically to 'enhance interoperability of government information systems.' The 2022 INN feasibility study explicitly targets interoperability of state information systems. The Senegal Services portal integrates multiple public services. However, full cross-system interoperability for the biometric ID is still under development (INN project ongoing; New Deal Technologique targets 'administrative interoperability' as a 2026 priority).

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for opening bank accounts and accessing financial services
Comments: Mandatory. AML/CFT Law (2018-03, amended 2024 as Law 02/2024) requires financial institutions to identify customers via reliable written documents before establishing a business relationship. The CNI is the primary acceptable ID document for banking KYC. BCEAO instructions require AML/KYC compliance for all WAEMU financial institutions. VOVE ID confirms 'National biometric ID rollout: 95% of adults now have a chip-enabled CNI' as a key enabler. Citizens need the national ID to obtain a bank account — it is functionally mandatory for financial services access.

Definition: Whether credentials are issued free of charge
Comments: No cost (free) for first-time or on-time applicants. The US State Department travel page states the national ID card fees are 'Free but for the new versions, there is a 10,000 CFA fee for anyone who didn't apply on time.' This means the credential is free for on-time enrolment, with a late fee of ~$16 USD for delayed applications. Standard enrolment is free for eligible citizens.

Definition: Whether the digital ID is recognized or interoperable across borders through regional agreements or travel documents
Value Name: Recognized in some regional contexts (e.g., ECOWAS travel)
Comments: Some regional recognition. Senegal was the first ECOWAS country to issue the ECOWAS National Biometric Identity Card (ENBIC) in October 2016. The ENBIC is accepted across ECOWAS member states as an ID and travel document, enabling free movement within the region (in lieu of a passport for ECOWAS travel). As of mid-2025, seven of 15 ECOWAS states have deployed ENBIC, making recognition regional but not universal globally. There is no formal bilateral interoperability outside ECOWAS.

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: Citizens aged 5 and above may apply. The IRB Canada (2018) document confirms: 'Any Senegalese citizen at least 5 years of age can apply for a national identity card.' The ID4Africa Iris Corporation document also states 'Available to citizens of Senegal who are at least 5 years of age.' The card is mandatory from age 15. This places eligibility in the 1–5 years band (Score 4: ages 1-5).

Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: Mandatory for some (citizens aged 15+). The IRB Canada document confirms the card is mandatory for all persons aged 15 and older. For those aged 5–14 it is optional (not mandatory but can be obtained). Wikipedia confirms 'Compulsory for all citizens. Biometric since 2017.' The ID4Africa document states it is 'mandatory for all persons aged 15 and older.' Thus it is mandatory for citizens 15+ but not for children under 15.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for accessing public healthcare services
Comments: Mandatory for subsidized/universal healthcare. Senegal's Couverture Sanitaire Universelle (CSU) uses biometric ID cards for healthcare access. The Al Jazeera report (Feb 2026) shows patients with biometric health cards get subsidized care while those without face uncertainty and full out-of-pocket costs. The LinkedIn/Better Than Cash Alliance analysis notes biometric ID is essential for 'identifying insured people' and accessing CSU subsidies. Senegal is 'rolling out biometric ID as part of its push toward universal healthcare' — effectively making it mandatory for subsidized health services.

Definition: Whether non-nationals including refugees, asylum seekers, and permanent residents are eligible to register
Comments: Some non-nationals are eligible. Foreign nationals residing in Senegal for more than 90 days must apply for a 'Carte d'Identité d'Étranger' (Foreign Identity Card), required from age 15 upwards. ECOWAS citizens can use their ECOWAS biometric ID card within Senegal. Refugees receive UNHCR documentation. However, not all non-nationals are eligible for the national CEDEAO biometric card — only Senegalese citizens receive the full national biometric ID.

Definition: Whether ID system undergoes regular security audits, penetration testing, or vulnerability assessments
Comments: No evidence of formal, systematic security reviews. The February 2026 ransomware breach of the DAF — which halted national ID card production — exposed significant security gaps. Dark Reading cited 'lack of security maturity.' The New Deal Technologique (2025) lists cybersecurity as a key priority, suggesting it was previously insufficient. No publicly documented formal security audits of the national ID system infrastructure were found. The breach investigation may prompt future reviews, but no completed security review programme has been documented.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for SIM card activation and mobile service registration
Comments: Mandatory. Since 2013 all SIM cards must be registered in Senegal. Biometric SIM registration (including fingerprints) has been enforced since then. The Prepaid SIM Card Wiki (updated 2026) confirms: 'Since 2013 all SIM cards officially are required to be registered and you even have to give a fingerprint.' In 2016, more than 5 million undocumented SIM cards were shut down by the regulator for non-compliance. Citizens need their national ID card to register a SIM. The biometric system directly links SIM registration to identity.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for registering for social assistance programs and accessing social services
Comments: Mandatory. The National Single Registry (Registre National Unique, RNU), which targets social safety net beneficiaries, uses identity verification through the CDP-regulated framework. Electricity and water connections require national ID. The INN feasibility study confirms ID is required for 'all public services.' The biometric health card (CMU) for Couverture Sanitaire Universelle uses biometric ID for beneficiary identification. Citizens without an ID face exclusion from subsidized services, as the Al Jazeera report (2026) illustrates.
